title: Getting Off the Tools: A Practical Guide for UK Builders
meta_description: A practical handover plan for UK builders: delegate site responsibilities, keep quality and client communication clear, and create time to run your business.
h1: Getting Off the Tools: A Practical Guide for UK Builders
hero_subtitle: Hand over site responsibilities in stages and create time to lead your building company.

intro.answer: Getting off the tools means building a team and a handover process that let you spend less time on manual work and more time running your building company, while keeping suitable oversight of delivery.

image.alt: A builder putting tools down to focus on running the business

intro.roadmap: This guide helps UK builders assess readiness, hand over one responsibility, trial protected management time and review what needs to improve before taking the next step.

briefing.title: Test Readiness Before You Step Back
briefing.intro: Start with one responsibility your team can take on with suitable support. Check capacity, agree decision limits and review the work before expanding the handover.

panels.heading: How do you know when you are ready to get off the tools?
paragraphs: Check how the work you currently do will be covered, including the time needed for supervision and training. Review the costs and workload before adding commitments.
Identify a capable person for the defined task. Check their capacity, give them the information they need and agree when to involve you.

panels.heading: Plan the handover in this order
paragraphs: A phased transition beats a clean break. Each step should prove itself before the next one starts.
steps: Name one responsibility and the person taking it on.
Agree the scope, decision limits, records and escalation route.
Demonstrate the task and work through it together.
Trial the handover with suitable oversight.
Review the result before expanding responsibility.

review.label: Watch for
review.text: If you keep being called back, record why. Missing information, unclear decisions and overloaded people need different solutions.

brief_before_heading: Start with the work that still depends on you
